item.title: AI security, post-quantum readiness, and assessments gain new SAF guidance — 15 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 15 November 2026

AI security, post-quantum readiness, and assessments gain new SAF guidance

The most consequential additions put concrete planning structure around the Security Adoption Framework (SAF): seven AI security control areas, cryptographic dependency discovery and quantum-resistant migration planning, and a documented workflow for reviewing Zero Trust Assessment results. Related pages map CIS Controls and Benchmarks, NIST CSF 2.0, and The Open Group Zero Trust model to SAF roles, disciplines, technologies, and implementation guidance. Updated Secure Future Initiative material emphasizes phishing-resistant authentication, managed identities, and secret and key lifecycle protection, while SecOps guidance adds incident governance, human oversight, and four implementation patterns.

Zero Trust · AI and agents

AI security guidance defines seven control areas

The new Secure AI with Zero Trust guidance covers AI applications, agents, identities, models, data, tools, and infrastructure. Its seven control areas span risk assessment and access control through monitoring and response, providing scope for AI inventories, lifecycle governance, least-privilege access, data protection, secure deployment, and activity monitoring.

Zero Trust · Strategy and deployment

Post-quantum guidance starts with cryptographic dependency discovery

New SAF guidance calls for identifying vulnerable cryptographic dependencies, planning quantum-resistant replacements, and maintaining readiness as standards and threats evolve. It addresses identity, applications, infrastructure, communications, IoT and OT, and supply-chain integrations, including harvest-now, decrypt-later exposure.

Zero Trust · General

Zero Trust assessment guidance documents review and handoff steps

The new page explains how to review reports across seven Zero Trust pillars, investigate skipped checks and errors, and optionally import mapped findings into Zero Trust Workshop task notes. It also documents report paths, prerequisites, data protections, and integration limitations.

Zero Trust · General

CIS mapping separates practice prioritization from configuration baselines

The new mapping distinguishes CIS Controls v8.1, used to prioritize security practices, from CIS Benchmarks, used for technology-specific configuration. It maps both to SAF roles, disciplines, technologies, and implementation guidance.

Secure Future Initiative · Identity and access

SFI identity guidance emphasizes phishing-resistant authentication and secret lifecycle

The updated guidance reframes identity and secret protection around reducing identity compromise, token abuse, and exposed-secret risk. It highlights phishing-resistant authentication, fewer static credentials, managed identities, automated key and secret lifecycle controls, standardized SDKs, and faster credential remediation.

item.title: SAF maps established security guidance into integrated, aligned, and companion resources — 8 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 8 November 2026

SAF maps established security guidance into integrated, aligned, and companion resources

A new Security Adoption Framework (SAF) article explains how existing Microsoft security guidance relates to SAF. It groups resources as integrated, SAF-aligned, or companion guidance and maps them to SAF disciplines.

Security adoption · General

SAF guidance mapping

The article organizes established Microsoft security resources into integrated, SAF-aligned, and companion categories, with mappings to SAF disciplines and related planning, architecture, implementation, and operations guidance.

item.title: SAF maps Zero Trust frameworks to disciplines, roles, capabilities, and implementation — 6 November 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 6 November 2026

SAF maps Zero Trust frameworks to disciplines, roles, capabilities, and implementation

The period centered on a substantive expansion and reorganization of Microsoft’s Security Adoption Framework guidance. New mapping guidance covers Zero Trust, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and the DoD Zero Trust Strategy, while related SAF material adds connections among business priorities, risk, responsibilities, implementation, and measurement. Two lower-impact updates refreshed titles and publication dates for MCRA and the SecOps workshop.

Security adoption · Standards and frameworks

New standards-to-SAF mappings

The new guidance maps security standards and framework objectives to SAF disciplines, roles, Microsoft security capabilities, and implementation guidance, including mappings for Zero Trust, the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model, and the DoD Zero Trust Strategy.

Security adoption · Standards and frameworks

SAF now links strategy through measurement

The SAF page now connects business priorities, risk, Zero Trust principles, security disciplines, technologies, and technical solutions, and adds guidance on shared responsibilities, implementation, measurement, and four connected framework components across hybrid, multicloud, and multiplatform environments.

Security adoption · General

SAF navigation shifts to goals and roles

“Using SAF effectively” now directs readers through tables organized around objectives and organizational roles, linking to strategy, architecture, disciplines, scenarios, technologies, workshops, and related guidance instead of the former top-down, build-up, and scenario-driven patterns.

Security adoption · General

MCRA title and publication date refreshed

The MCRA page and heading now omit “Review,” and its publication date is shown as November 6, 2026, replacing November 2.

Security operations · Strategy and deployment

SecOps workshop naming and date updated

The Microsoft Zero Trust Workshop page now uses “SecOps” capitalization in its title and heading, and its page date changed from May 24 to November 6, 2026.

View all updates for 6 November 2026 →
